I'm checking whether the casting step in upstream scatter drops the time unit by converting values to their physical representation before casting to the target dtype. That would explain why the datetime, duration, and date results come out shifted by the unit mismatch.

I'm checking the scatter path's conversion logic: the values get converted to their physical representation before being cast to the target dtype, which is where the unit gets lost. Casting to the logical dtype first and only then taking the physical form would avoid that, though I'm not certain how upstream handles timezone-aware targets.

I'm tracing the by-grouped asof path, where the left rows may be split into partitions that each keep their own group state, so the result depends on how the rows are chunked.

I'm tracing how the streaming engine handles the categorical keys, since its result of `["b","d",None,None,None]` doesn't match the plain physical-code backward join I just worked out, so something else must alter the keys or the right side before the join runs. I'll check how the asof lowering sets up its temporary key columns.
